items.name: Google Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Carbon, announced October 28, is its strongest frontier model yet, built for long-horizon engineering and cybersecurity defence: it ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (59) and leads SEC-bench Pro (88.2%), ExploitGym (54.8%) and CWE-bench (71.0%). It is rolling out first to a subset of cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens introductory pricing.

items.name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
items.summary: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, released October 28, is an open-weight speech model that combines transcription in 40 languages, translation in 31 languages, speaker attribution for up to eight speakers, and audio question-answering in a single checkpoint. It ships alongside Granary v2, an open data-curation pipeline covering 463,062 hours of speech across 48 languages.

items.name: Google DeepMind Genie 4
items.summary: Google DeepMind's Genie 4, announced October 27, is a world model that generates interactive, photorealistic simulated environments in real time, with native audio — music, ambient sound and character dialogue — generated alongside the scene. Users steer it with keyboard controls and natural-language prompts; it is rolling out first as a research preview for trusted testers, then to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie.

items.name: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI's fast everyday-work model, launched October 26, combines visual reasoning with precise computer use and clearer writing at 50% lower standard API prices than GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol. It is available in ChatGPT Work and Codex and via the API as gpt-6.1-terra, and OpenAI says it finishes tasks over 3x faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol.
